rules.title: California Statewide Rent Cap
rules.quote: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
rules.summary: Landlords may not increase rent more than 5% plus the local CPI or 10%, whichever is lower, in any 12-month period.
rules.effective_date_evidence: This section shall become operative on April 1, 2024.
rules.effective_until_evidence: This section shall remain in effect until January 1, 2030, and as of that date is repealed.

related_citations.evidence: Repealed (in Sec. 3) and added by Stats. 2023, Ch. 290, Sec. 4. (SB 567) Effective January 1, 2024.
This property is not subject to the rent limits imposed by Section 1947.12 of the Civil Code and is not subject to the just cause requirements of Section 1946.2 of the Civil Code.

rules.coverage_text: Exemptions include: affordable housing, dorms, units under local rent control with stricter limits, housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years (except mobilehomes), single-family homes and condos owned by non-corporate entities with proper notice, duplexes where owner occupies one unit.
rules.exemption_note: Housing subject to rent control with lower caps is exempt; single-family homes and condos owned by individuals/non-corporate entities are exempt if proper notice provided; owner-occupied duplexes exempt.
rules.penalty: Tenant may sue for injunctive relief, actual damages for excess rent paid, reasonable attorney's fees and costs, and up to triple damages if owner acted willfully or with oppression, fraud, or malice. Attorney General, city attorney, or county counsel may also enforce and seek injunctive relief.
